title: Multimodal Pragmatic Jailbreak on Text-to-image Models

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating text-to-image models' Attack Success Rate (ASR) for generating racially offensive multimodal memes by combining seemingly benign images of racial/ethnic groups with targeted visual text (e.g., 'sea monkeys' text rendered over an image of Black children).
Measuring the frequency of text-to-image models generating offensive multimodal content by pairing religious imagery (e.g., Sikh turbans) with derogatory visual text.
Assessing model vulnerability to generating homophobic content by pairing LGBTQ+ symbols (e.g., pride flags) with insulting visual text.
Evaluating the generation of anti-immigrant multimodal content by combining specific imagery (e.g., camouflage and guns) with visual text targeting immigrants.
Testing the generation of sexist multimodal content by pairing images of women in professional settings with misogynistic or stereotyping visual text (e.g., 'always in the kitchen').
Measuring the generation of ableist content by combining images of individuals with physical disabilities with mocking visual text.
Assessing the generation of ageist content by combining images of elderly individuals with mocking or stereotypical visual text.
Evaluating the generation of offensive political satire by combining animal imagery with visual text mocking specific political voters.
